notes:
Fixed:
- A video whose duration could not be read is no longer refused: Render H264/H265, Intro/Outro/Logo, Loop and Split now run anyway and show elapsed time instead of a percentage. Files with no duration header (MPEG-TS, FLV, some MKV) and files still being written render exactly as before
- Split (exact mode) without a known duration stops at the first empty part and removes it, instead of not starting at all
- Trim only needs the duration when "trim from end" is enabled; trimming from the start alone now runs to the end of the file
- "Error: Invalid Duration" now says WHY in the clickable error popup: ffprobe's own message (e.g. "moov atom not found" for a recording that was never closed), a missing or unreadable file, or ffprobe/ffmpeg not being installed. The Copy button finally has something worth pasting
- Chroma Key still needs the video length (the green screen loops forever, so it is what bounds the output) and now explains that in the error
- Loop's "Invalid Duration Format" names the value it rejected and the format it expects (HH:MM:SS)

Changed:
- Running rows show "Processing... 1:15" (elapsed) when no percentage can be computed
